registry.go is the only file containing prompt text; each entry has id, kind, apps, catalog keys, applies-when, default, required fragments and a fixed output schema, with a typed handle Prompt[V] and NoVars for entries without variables.
User-authored text (smart-script bodies, workflow stage and step prompts), tool and server names, tool error strings and result data formatting are not in the prompt registry.

Prompt entry kinds are system, message, suffix, instructions, tool, argument, toolResult and fragment; an argument is one MCP tool property description carrying Parent tool and Field, and a fragment is included via {{template}}.
InputSchema[T] sets each tool property's description from its argument entry, a mismatch panics at server build, and jsonschema:"..." tags are not used.
Prompt templates use text/template, one set per resolve, with only the funcs inc and join; an entry with NoVars and no fragments is literal and never parsed.
Default prompts render byte-identical to the pre-P271 output, checked against testdata/golden.
RenderParts wraps each string variable in marker runes and splits so Settings Preview can mark resolved values with VarText; a failed self-check returns one literal part.

Prompt overrides are stored per app in <home>/llm-prompts.json (~/.kira-studio/ or ~/.kira-space/), written with renameio at mode 0600, shaped {version, revision, overrides: {id: {text, defaultHash, updatedAt}}}.
Saving the default text removes the override; override text must be 1 byte to 32 KiB.
A prompt change carries baseHash, and a stale change is refused with E_CONFLICT.

Server-side validation requires the template to parse, every prompt:"required" variable to be referenced, every required fragment to be included, and execution against example vars to succeed.
The memory.dataHygiene fragment is required in memory system prompts as an injection defence.

dbmcp and claudeheadless rebuild their MCP server when Revision() changes.
memory-mcp (stdio subprocess) builds instructions and tool/argument descriptions once per process, so edits apply only to new Claude sessions (newSession in Settings).
